expectations.text: Applies the reasoning to Python/backend (does NOT give React- or hook-specific advice)
expectations.evidence: FastAPI package layout: router.py/schemas.py/models.py/repository.py/service.py/discounts.py. No React/hook advice.

expectations.text: Recommends a real abstraction (pure function / service / repository) over reflexive file-splitting
expectations.evidence: 'discounts.py — the business logic ... Make it pure functions'; repository behind named functions like get_order_by_id; service.py orchestration.

expectations.text: Co-locates tightly coupled handler+logic; separates only cleanly-standalone layers (e.g. discount calc or DB access)
expectations.evidence: Reflexively splits all four+ concerns into separate files; explicitly pulls schemas away from handlers ('Keeping these separate from the ORM models is the important one'). Does not co-locate the coupled handler+schemas.

expectations.text: Applies the understood-in-isolation test and/or the ~300-line guidance to the module
expectations.evidence: No isolation test; treats 250 lines as already split-worthy ('At ~250 lines you're right at the point where the package pays off'), not applying the ~300-line keep-together guidance.
